name: Family-Based Immigration (Immediate Relatives & Preference Categories)

requirement_groups.name: Immediate relatives of US citizens (no annual cap)

requirements.blocker_text: This covers spouses (IR-1/CR-1), children (IR-2), and parents (IR-5) of US citizens — no annual numerical cap applies to this category.

value.note: sponsor income at least 125% of the Federal Poverty Guidelines (100% for active-duty military sponsoring a spouse/child)

requirements.blocker_text: This requires the sponsor to file Form I-864 (Affidavit of Support) showing income at least 125% of the Federal Poverty Guidelines (100% for active-duty military sponsoring a spouse/child).
requirements.fix_path: Meet the income threshold, or secure a joint sponsor who does.

requirements.blocker_text: This covers unmarried adult children of citizens (F1), spouses/children/unmarried adult children of LPRs (F2A/F2B), married children of citizens (F3), and siblings of adult citizens (F4) — each subject to annual worldwide and per-country numerical limits, creating multi-year to multi-decade backlogs depending on category and country of birth.

evidence_required.document: Affidavit of Support (Form I-864) meeting the income threshold
Evidence of the qualifying family relationship

outcome.duration_length: indefinite — direct green card for immediate relatives; preference categories wait for priority date to become current

sources.title: Form I-864, Affidavit of Support - USCIS

notes: GENUINE STRUCTURAL BIFURCATION worth flagging prominently: immediate relatives face NO annual cap and pr_after_months is genuinely 0 (subject only to processing time), while preference categories face severe per-country backlogs — the Aug 2026 Visa Bulletin shows F1/F2A/F2B/F3/F4 for Mexico and the Philippines running years to decades behind other countries (e.g. F4 Mexico dated back to April 2001, a 25-year-old priority date). pr_after_months (0) is accurate only for the immediate-relatives group; the preference-categories group has no fixed figure since it depends entirely on category and country of birth — the single largest per-country variance encoded in any route across this entire dataset. I-864 income threshold is formula-based (125% of the current Federal Poverty Guidelines, updated annually — commonly around March) but exact current dollar tables by household size weren't independently confirmed at tier-1 precision during the research this was built from; encoded as the percentage rule rather than a specific dollar figure to avoid a stale/wrong number.
